When it is operated in the grid connected mode, it is connected to the grid at the point of common coupling (PCC). A micro grid normally consists of renewable energy sources, a diesel generator, storage facilities and a central controller. The micro grid described in this paper contains only a diesel generator, a wind emulator and the loads. Designing of central controller is the main objective of this research. This paper discuss how the governor of the diesel generator is controlled via a central controller in both the isolated and grid connected operations. Frequency should be controlled in isolated operation and the power flow through point of common coupling (PCC) should be controlled in the grid connected operation. MATLAB Simulink was used to simulate and analyze both of these situations. This paper discusses how it was used for generating the required result in order to accomplish the mentioned task.

articleTitle: Analysis and study of Zeta converter fed by solar photovoltaic array
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Due to the increasing demand of electricity and the limited conventional energy resources, Solar Photovoltaic energy becomes a favorable alternative as it is pollution free, freely available and has less maintenance cost. This paper presents basic steady state analysis of Zeta Converter by using State Space Averaging Method in continuous inductor current mode. The Zeta converter is a fourth order DC-DC converter which is capable of operating in Buck and Boost Mode. The Zeta Converter is cascaded between Solar Photovoltaic Panel and Load. The input voltage to Zeta converter is fed by a photovoltaic panel. The modeling of solar panel is done by considering the design equation of photon current and reverses saturation current. The objective of this paper is to analyze the performance of Zeta converter by a change in Temperature, Irradiance, Duty Cycle and Load Resistance. The effectiveness of model with the result is verified by using simulation done in MATLAB™ Simulink.

articleTitle: Power flow control of dfig generators for wind turbine variable speed using STATCOM
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper presents to generate reference voltage for a static compensator (STATCOM) operating in voltage-control mode. The proposed the individual wind turbine using STSTCOM of dynamic wind farm electric network, of a Power Flow Control of DFIG Generators for Wind Turbine Variable Speed using STATCOM is connected to the grid. The control capability of the wind farm that is a critical issue in paining and working of the wind system. The dc link capacitor to exchange the power with the three phase feeders, the power-quality issues by providing load balancing and voltage regulation on the load can be satisfied with the proposed method.

articleTitle: A four terminal transmission line protection by wavelet approach in the presence of SVC using hybrid generation
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Modern electric supply systems are invariably three phase. The design of transmission and distribution networks is such that normal operations reasonably close to the balanced three phase working conditions to give a complete analysis. A compound generation is a segment of power system in which number of sources commonly attached to a power electronic converter and loads are associated to operate independently. The protection of multi terminal transmission lines is a challenging task due to possible in feed or out feed currents contributed from the tapped lines. The protection scheme is crucial against faults based on traditional over current protection since there are adequate problems due to fault currents in the mode of operation. This paper proposes a novel approach for detection, discrimination of the faults and a control paradigm for four terminal transmission line protection, in presence of PV and wind sources. It deals about transient current based protection scheme for SVC compensated multi terminal transmission system with discrete wavelet transform. Fault indices of all phase currents at all terminals are obtained by analyzing the detail coefficients of current signals using bior 1.5 mother wavelet. This method is analyzed for different types of faults and is found effective for detection and discrimination of fault with various fault inception angle and fault impedance.

articleTitle: Third method for regenerative braking in matrix converter drive: More electric aircraft
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper describes a novel method for braking regeneration in the Matrix Converter (MC) drive is proposed, called Standard Clamp Circuit (SCC) method for More Electric Aircraft (MEA). In earlier publications, Bi-Directional Switch (BDS) method and Input Power Clamp (IPC) method with Power Comparison (PC) technique and Input Voltage Reference (IVR) technique for regenerative braking or electrical braking in the Matrix Converter drive have been discussed. The electrical braking is important in many aerospace applications such as surface actuation and Air to Air (in-flight) refueling system. Therefore, the inherent regeneration capability of the Matrix Converter drive is not desirable for aerospace applications so it has to be avoided. In contrast to earlier methods, the proposed SCC method is using the existing standard clamp circuit in the Matrix Converter drive. The proposed methods are demonstrated through detailed simulation results.

articleTitle: Monitoring the thermal behavior of induction motor using regression technique
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: To insure an efficient operation of an electrical machine, its thermal aspects has to be dealt apart from the Electromagnetic parameters. The rise in temperature of an electrical machine depends mainly on the temperature rise in the motor winding. Here a new method is proposed for measuring and predicting the temperature rise in stator winding. Real-Time Thermal Data is recorded using temperature sensor interfaced with arduino microcontroller during the heat run test conducted on the machine. Using this, a set of generalized equations are derived through curve fitting technique to predict the temperature rise in an winding at any load and timing conditions. In this paper, the above technique is employed for a 5 H.P 3-phase Slip ring Induction Machine and the results are validated with the temperature measured using embedded sensors.

articleTitle: A COMSOL approach to the analysis of a micro-scale piezoelectric cantilever beam: The effect of dimension parameters on the eigen frequency
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Eigen frequency is one of the most important system responses to be considered while designing a micro-scale piezoelectric cantilever beam. This paper investigates and analyzes the effect of dimension parameters of a micro-scale piezoelectric cantilever beam on its eigen frequency. The beam is assumed to be made of silicon. Structural mechanics based finite element analysis is carried out in the environment of COMSOL multiphysics software for the study. It is seen that length and thickness have continuous effect on the eigen frequency; whereas, the effect of width is discontinuous.

articleTitle: Design and hardware implementation of 8051 micro-controller based single-phase inverter
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper presents 8051 micro-controller based design and hardware implementation of a single-phase inverter using Metal-Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistors (MOSFET) as switch and analyzes its output responses. The inverter comprises of two parts: the control (driver) circuit and the power circuit. The control circuit performs the operation of generating the gate pulses to trigger the MOSFETs. The multiple pulse width modulation (MPWM) technique has been implemented and the triggering pulses are obtained by the microcontroller 8051. The power circuit is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment for harmonic analysis purpose. A laboratory prototype is also designed and tested with different loading conditions. Results show the effectiveness of MPWM technique based single-phase inverter. The snubber design parameters are also calculated for high current inductive load and are tested for the designed prototype. The dead-band in the switching pulses, which is conventionally provided by a dead-band circuit cascaded to a pulse generator along with a dead band circuit, is now generated using 8051 micro-controller kit. This leads to reduced hardware components requirement and hence reduced cost. This way the paper gives an idea about the low—cost design estimation which has got significant low power domestic applications.

articleTitle: Lighting audit and energy efficient LED based lighting scheme for a pharmaceutical industry
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Artificial lighting is a visible source of energy consumption in any industries. Providing an energy efficient lighting is the only way by which the energy consumption can be minimized. Energy efficient solution should not compromise with the lighting requirement in terms of Lux levels when trying to reduce the electric load and energy consumption. Hence the lighting solution should be proposed in such a way to keep the required illumination levels by the use of low power consuming fixtures. This paper presents the results of a lighting audit done on a pharmaceutical industry located at Chennai, India and proposes an energy efficient lighting solution to cope up with the short comings. The project is carried out by conducting an initial survey of the site to acquire details of pharmaceutical industry like the existing lighting system, illumination levels and patterns, different areas and their functionalities etc. With the acquired details, the existing lighting system is simulated in lighting simulation software called DIALux. A new lighting strategy is proposed in terms of lux levels and energy consumption in order to minimise the total energy requirement of the building. Energy efficient lighting solutions not only reduces the energy consumption but also helps in reducing the carbon footprint.

articleTitle: AGC of multi-area ST — thermal — hydro system incorporating redox flow batteries
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In present article, the impact of redox flow batteries (RFB) in suppressing the oscillations of three unequal area system including solar thermal system in area1 is presented. Various classical controllers namely integral (I), proportionalintegral (PI) and proportional-integral-derivative (PID) are applied as supplementary controllers independently. The nature inspired optimization method named moth-flame optimization (MFO) technique is applied to optimize the various parameters of I, PI and PID controllers. Studies explores that PID controller provides improved dynamic responses than others in settling time and cost function value. Simulation analysis reveals the effectiveness of MFO over genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization techniques. Further, it is seen that PID controller in presence of RFB units effectively minimizes the oscillations against both step load and random perturbations. Sensitivity analysis shows that PID controller parameters found at nominal conditions are insensitive to wide changes in governor and turbine time constants of thermal units.

articleTitle: Dynamic modelling of a double-cage induction machine for analysis with WECS
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a 7th order and a 5th order model for a double-cage induction machine that can be used in the context of power system analysis involving wind eneregy conversion systems (WECS). Through a series of case studies a comparison is made between the double- and single-cage models of an induction machine to show that the double-cage structure offers higher starting torque characteristics. Further, it is shown that at low frequency oscillations which are dominant in power swing studies, both the models behave almost identically.

articleTitle: Mitigation of current harmonics in renewable source integrated grid topology with fuzzy based dynamic shunt active filter
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Growing population and industrialization demanding more power from the electrical utility. This causes drastic changes in the utility structure. The non conventional sources replaces the signing off conventional sources. The integration of non conventional sourses and different loads, hinders the power quality of the system. This paper uses Dynamic Shunt Active Fiter (DSAF) to mitigate the current hormonics and integrates the Renewable Energy units to grid. The controller performance is studied with conventional PI & Fuzzy technique. The proposed system performance is studied in MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Accurate phasor estimation during power swing
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In a power system network, the detection of fault during power oscillation is one of the major issues of concern. The behavior of voltages and currents in a fault is same during a power swing. A Power Swing Blocking technology by using phasor analysis can be used to differentiate between a fault and power swing. By using this technique, the detection of fault is possible during power swing whether it is symmetrical or asymmetrical fault. Here, in 2 bus system, the fault with different fault resistances are simulated through PSCAD Software to test this technology. The proposed method is very fast and accurate.

articleTitle: A novel flux lock type superconducting FCL in a wind energy system applications
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Now a days, Superconducting fault current limiter (SFCL) is emerged as one of the most accomplished fault current limiter (FCL) In this Paper, a Novel Flux lock type Superconducting FCL in a wind energy system applications is limiting the fault current in wind energy system. The proposed Resistive and flux lock type based super conducting FCLS have improved performance in terms of current limitation is reduced. Superconducting FCLs appears as an excellent FCL which tends to satisfy above features. The whole research work and analysis has been carried out in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment for isolated wind energy system.

articleTitle: Mac protocols for reduced power consumption in Intra-cluster design for wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) are finding its applications in almost all areas especially in Industries where reduced power conservation is the prime concern and protocols following reduced energy are needed. Medium Access Protocols (MAC) plays a very important role in energy conservation. This paper gives a brief introduction of MAC protocols, their classification and how Intra-Cluster communication takes place. A classification of few protocols is explained in detail. Clustering is an ideal way of organizing a network for reduced energy consumption. Intra-Cluster communication plays a key role in total energy consumption of the overall network. Therefore strategies involved in Intra-Cluster communication become very essential and the design should be flexible and energy-conservative.

articleTitle: Energy detection with different digital modulation techniques over Rayleigh fading channels in cognitive radio networks
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The sensing of radio spectrum is an essential problem in cognitive radio(CR) networks, where secondary users (SUs) need to detect the presence of primary users (PUs) before they use the spectrum allocated to PUs. The detection of primary user status and the spectrum sensing are the major issues in cognitive radio systems. We employ one of the simplest and most efficient Spectrum Sensing technique, the Energy Detection(ED) with three different digital modulation techniques BPSK, QPSK, 16-QAM. In this paper, we analyze the performance of the Energy Detection technique with BPSK, QPSK, 16-QAM modulation techniques over Rayleigh fading Channel. Further, we analyze the performance and BER (Bit Error Rate) of ED under Rayleigh fading and AWGN channels. The investigation and analysis on Energy Detection with above digital modulation techniques can be utilized for future reference of spectrum sensing in the CR networks over AWGN and Rayleigh fading channels.

articleTitle: Mitigation of voltage disturbances using fuzzy logic controller in a grid connected DFIG for different types of fault
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Renewable Energy has a consistent share in today's scenario and its contribution is very significant. It is highly mandatory to synchronise wind energy system with the grid. In doubly fed induction generator (DFIG), stator and rotor connections differs from that of a normal synchronous generators. The rotor gives pulse at a constant rate to maintain its voltage and frequency same as that of the grid. In the proposed scheme, there are two converter topologies involved. one converter is placed near the rectifier side and the other converter is placed near the inverter sides. The fuzzy based control scheme is used to regulate the voltage with respect to dc link capacitor and also removes the oscillations to the maximum extent. Various fault conditions are simulated and analysed by means of MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Operating an alert system using facial expression
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Facial expression is become a prominent way of understanding people. In past many decades many people have been attracted to this field of image processing as it helps in many of the real time application. Currently, there have been many applications which are based on human facial expression recognition. One of its application is controlling the music player on the basis of human emotions and moods. In this work a system is developed which can help in reducing the rate of crime caused due to anger. Here the focus will be to calculate the human emotions and transfer this data to the responsible organization which can take some instance step to avoid crime. The system process works in java. This application which is based on detecting human facial expressions will be used to operate an alert system that is very much needed to reduce the crime rate. It can reduce the crime rate worldwide by sending alerts to nearby police stations so that people won't become victim of any crime. This application is purely bases on detecting facial expression of people because it is easy to read the different kind of emotions on the human face. This data of expressions will be used to train a system so that this application can be used in a system to detect facial expressions.

articleTitle: Impact of DG on locational marginal price under multi constrained environment
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: During the nineties decade, many electric utilities and power network companies all around the world intended to change their mode of operation and business, from vertically integrated structure to open market systems. The power sector is evolving into a distributed and competitive industry in which market forces drive the price of electricity and reduce the net cost through increased competition. Competition in the electric power industry will promote utilities to become more efficient and reduce costs in order to lower the electricity prices. Under this deregulated environment, determination of market clearing price (MCP) is one of the important function of a pool operator. In this context, location based price structure became an efficient method for electricity pricing. The Locational Marginal Price (LMP) changes with different parameters such as operational, line design and generator design parameters. The impacts of Locational Marginal Price with respect to different combination of constraints, and comparison of LMP with and without Distributed Generation are discussed in this paper. Distributed generation is modelled at the load buses by injecting necessary MW and the impact is analyzed after running the optimal power flow. The study about the combinational effects of constraints will give more insight to the pricing structure and helps to improve the system's efficient operation. IEEE standard 9 bus system is taken as the test system and LMP is simulated on the Power World Simulator software.

articleTitle: Electric DC WIPS: All electric aircraft
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper deals with design, modeling and validation of More Open Electrical Technologies (MOET) and improvements in the utilization of electric power systems of the aircraft for addressing the concept of All Electric Aircraft (AEA) or More Electric Aircraft (MEA) with respect to Wings Ice Protection Systems (WIPS). Here the pneumatic power is replaced with electric power for Wings Ice Protection Systems (WIPS). The electric DC WIPS protects the aircraft against the build-up of ice on its structures. There are two ways: 1) Anti-Ice 2) De-Ice. The electric DC WIPS is designed to consume 68.9Kw maximum power at 270 VDC range, means 54.6kW for Anti-ice and 14.3kW for De-ice. The detailed simulation results are presented to prove the proposed electric DC WIPS concept with novel power control technique.

articleTitle: Simulation of three-phase two-stage grid connected photovoltaic system using Cuk converter
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper proposes the grid connected photovoltaic system (GCPVS). In this paper, two-stage GCPVS presents which consists of inverter and dc-dc converter (Cuk converter). We know that two stage means there are converter and inverter both in system. The paper suggests design and PV simulation in MATLAB for two stages system. The pulse width modulation (PWM) is applied on the inverter to synchronizing the current with the Grid voltage in the system. In two-stage, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm is connected to the dc-to-dc converter which extracts high power from MPPT. This paper deals with simulation of two-stage GCPVS in MATLAB with the simulated results.

articleTitle: A feasibility study of low voltage DC distribution system for LED lighting in building
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: An analysis is presented to show the techno-economical benefit of low voltage DC (LVDC) distribution to the lighting system in building through Solar Photovoltaic (PV) system. The proposed DC distribution system is considered by replacing conventional T8 linear fluorescent light (LFL) to LED light achieving improved efficiency powered by solar energy. The result shows that 60% capacity of load is reduced, saving 1051.2 MWh electricity which is mitigated 704.304 ton CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission by paying back at 9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> year of the project cost for the 20 year period Life Cycle Cost (LCC) analysis.

articleTitle: Optimal location and parameters of GUPFC for transmission loss minimization using PSO algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Transmission losses are one of the major losses faced by our power system. Reduction of transmission losses will benefit us by saving a large amount of power. The transmission losses can be reduced by placing FACTS devices in the power system. Among all the FACTS devices Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) and Generalized Unified Power Flow Controller (GUPFC) are the best. Incorporating the GUPFC in to the power system and placing it to the optimal location and setting its output to optimal values can reduce the transmission losses. This paper explains the way to locate the optimal location of GUPFC and finding the optimal setting using PSO algorithm to reduce the total transmission losses. Voltage variation is taken as the criteria for finding the location and PSO is used for finding the settings of GUPFC. This study is conducted on an IEEE 14-bus system using MATLAB software.

articleTitle: A review on enhancing fault ride-through capability of distributed generation in a microgrid
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Although the introduction of distributed generation (DG) in a distribution system improves the power quality of power system, it increases the fault current level reducing voltage at point of common-coupling (PCC). Hence, there is a need of improving fault ride-through (FRT) capability to avoid sudden tripping of DG units from the utility grid during voltage sag in a faulty condition. This paper provides an overview of distributed generation and its impact on distribution system operation. The novel feature of this paper is to study a new concept called FRT requirements and various methods for enhancing FRT capability.

articleTitle: Mathematical modelling and investigation of reduced order induction motor drive system
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This project presents a platform for research in digital simulation applications which are on the way to replace the partial scale or full scale validation requirement of physical systems. The modeling of inverter fed electric drive has been done and the results have been simulated. In this topology, the inverter is coupled with the induction machine and solved symbolically in MATLAB/SIMULINK. Simultaneously a reduced order model has also been developed and modeled using the same graphic user interface. This project intends to provide an accurate comparison of the two models, their industrial applications as well as their research applications. Interfacing of Simulations can also be done with industrial controllers, which saves huge economic cost and allowing an economic tool for testing of drive controller and offering the flexibility require to simulate machine in every power range. The validation of proposed algorithm and models has been done in the MATLAB environment. Evaluation is done on the basis of accuracy, zero crossing and step size where the performance and working of electric dive system is observed.

articleTitle: Dynamic hand gesture recognition using Kinect
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In dynamic hand gesture recognition, the separation of hand part from the surroundings and locating the exact position of the hand has always been one of the major problems. In this paper we propose a simple and fast method to capture the trajectory of the moving hand and compare it with the trajectories corresponding to different gestures in the database to recognize the gesture performed using Dynamic Time Warping. For this process, a device called Kinect by Microsoft is used to provide depth map using infrared sensor for the hand part separation from the surrounding. The experimental results show that the method proposed succeeds in locating the position of the hand in each frame. Implementation of this process was done using MATLAB.

articleTitle: A practical approach for optimal allocation of dispatchable and non-dispatchable DG units in distribution systems
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The optimal allocation of distributed generation (DG) units results in active power loss reduction and voltage profile improvement in distribution systems. Loss sensitivity factor is utilized to identify the optimal candidate locations of DG. To determine the optimal capacity of DG units the analytical expressions are used. A fast computational method is obtained by combining both these methods together. To validate the suitability of the intended method, it has been applied to IEEE 33-bus test distribution system and also employed on a practical distribution feeder.

articleTitle: Automated video object recognition system
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Curiosity to know the unknown and desire to behold what we need are important reasons for advancement in technology. Humans had the ability of vision to know what the world is like and through which we were able to explore and visualize the unknown and the needed respectively. As its result, computer vision was introduced to the world at late 1970's which was a field which consists of various discipline. This was developed to automate the process of what human visual system can perform. It concentrates on the theory of artificial intelligence which uses images as source of information. There are multiple forms to represent image data such as video sequence, views from multiple camera or multi-dimensional data from the medical scanner etc. In this article, the video which has been used for surveillance and entertainment has been studied in various perspective of its application. Thus, under computer vision the video could be explicitly used for newer implementation and experiments where they could be enhanced to a lot more than just a visual source.

articleTitle: Droop reference based decoupling coupling control of NPC inverter for islanded microgrid
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The Increasing demand of clean energy has evoked huge interest in microgrid that uses renewable energy sources like solar, wind, fuel cell and control of microgrid components such as inverters. The neutral point clamped multilevel inverters have gained prominence due to its substantial advantage of power quality in islanded mode and coupling at a common point of main grid in grid connected. The islanded operation of microgrid necessitates frequency and voltage regulation based on the filter inductance current and capacitor voltage. The paper investigates the droop based decoupling control of neutral point clamped 3-level inverter in islanded mode of operation of microgrid. The control strategy is carried out in rotating reference frame. The set reference for the control strategy is generated by regulation of real and reactive power. The proposed control strategy is accomplished in Matlab Simulink environment and results were analyzed.

articleTitle: Enhancement of power system performance with SVC-DFIG in 140 — bus system
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper proposes a reactive power management analysis of the power electronic converters for grid-connected system. Power system stability affected by impedance of a Transmission line, Line Faults and various RLC load power losses. The power electronic based Controllers examined are: Thyristor controlled Reactor (TCR) + Multiples of Thyristor Switched Capacitor (TSC) or the Static VAR Compensator (SVC) and doubly fed induction generator. The aim is to determine which bus yields the highest demand of reactive power to improve voltage stability to overcome power losses of the conductor per line length with a predetermined voltage and optimum location of multiples of SVC. In view of this, a furled commercial Static VAR compensator model is developed and used to generate power for different load conditions. Afterwards, a relation between the various configurations TSC is established to evaluate the stability of the power system. The power loss model presented in this paper has taken into account the conduction and load power losses within the power system. The analysis reveals that Enhancement of power system performance with SVC managed reactive power network and voltage stabilisation considered in this research. It is shown that SVC controller with multiples of TSC has the dominant effect on the system considerably improved grid reliability, availability and Stability. This research indicates multiple TSC is a much better option for grid-connected DFIG based wind energy conversion 140 bus system.

articleTitle: Eye blinking detection for the detection of computer vision syndrome
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Computers have become a vital part of our workplaces. Millions of computer users spend at least more than two hours in front of a computer screen daily. This excessive use of computers leads to a disorder known as “Computer Vision Syndrome”. Most of the computer users suffer from CVS. CVS causes irritation, redness of the user's eye. CVS directly affects productivity of a computer user and user becomes prone to make mistakes and hence, this is a serious issue for people working in industrial sector. In this paper, we have proposed a method based on feature extraction methods such as SURF and Harris corner detection to detect the uncharacteristic behavior of a human eye and prevent CVS by providing alerts. The proposed method provides highly accurate results.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna embedded with circular split ring resonator for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper presents a design methodology for producing a probe feed patch antenna embedded with circular split ring resonator using Ansoft HFSS design environment. A co-axial probe feed is used to excite the patch antenna since it exhibits a low spurious radiation and is easy to match. In general, to achieve size reduction the slots are cut in a rectangular patch which ultimately leads to the impedance mismatch. Therefore a circular split ring resonator is embedded inside the slot. A sub-wave length resonance can be accomplished with a good impedance match, return loss, VSWR and antenna gain due to the geometry of circular split ring resonator. It is evident from the results that the proposed antenna designed on Rogers RT/duroid 5880, resonates at 5.9 GHz with a gain of 6.2dBi, VSWR 1.1 and return loss -33.2dB.

articleTitle: Word spotting techniques for Indian scripts: A survey
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Word spotting based techniques for document image retrieval have recently become very popular especially in Indian scripts because of lack of accurate OCR systems. Some notable work has been reported for word spotting in various Indian scripts like Devanagari, Malayalam, Bangla, and Telugu. However, there does not exist any summary and comparison of work reported for Indian scripts using recognition free approach. This paper discusses the architecture of recognition free approach and provides a comprehensive survey of word spotting techniques for different Indian scripts.

articleTitle: Embedded system based intelligent demand side management in smart grid
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Peak Demands are the foremost problems in today's electricity sector as thirst for power consumption proliferates whereas the peak demand makes it difficult to meet the increased demand of electricity. This paper focuses on autonomous peak demand management through GSM based intelligent monitoring system. In this automated system real time data acquisition of daily power consumption has been connected to base station through GSM network for suspending maximum peak demand. This proposed intellectual system has been demonstrated on a model which is designed for a maximum peak demand of 500W. The intended scheme will be contributing towards its expansion of application in smart grid environment.

articleTitle: Battery powered 4-phase 8/6 pole SRM drive for advanced electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: A growing need for “electric vehicles” against fuel consumption and pollution is seen all around the world. Unlike vehicles with combustion engines, battery powered electric vehicles do not produce exhaust gases during operation. There is no fuel odor and these vehicles are silent. These features itself makes battery powered electric vehicles more environment friendly than vehicles with conventional technologies. Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) has gained its importance in variable speed control operations as it has advantages like constructional simplicity, high starting torque, no magnets or windings on the rotor and adaptability to hostile conditions. In this paper, a four phase SRM drive operated with hysteresis control is shown which can be used to drive an electric vehicle. Hysteresis control is used for low speed operations so that this simple control can be used in electric vehicles specially designed for metro purposes. MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation results are presented for this control strategy.

articleTitle: Phasor estimation methods in the presence of harmonics and noise: A comparative analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Frequency is an important parameter that plays a crucial role in the monitoring, protection and control of power system. It provides an indication of the interconnection's generation/load balance. Normally nominal frequency is either 50 Hz or 60 Hz in most of the countries. Any deviation of frequency from nominal is an indication of abnormal condition or generation/load imbalance. Synchronized phasor measurement unit (PMUs) are providing a promising future for accurate phasor and frequency estimation. Initially Synchrophasor estimation was the main thrust and after amendments in IEEE standards researchers could able to provide solution for frequency and rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) estimation. The main concern now is to achieve accurate, fast, less computationally complex and economic frequency and ROCOF estimation algorithm. So far different algorithms have been proposed for commercial PMUs and are being claimed as in compliance with IEEE standards C37.118.2011. These standards are providing benchmark for justifying accuracy of commercial PMUs. For effective monitoring and control of these PMUs, their operation under transient and large dynamic oscillation demands quick and highly accurate estimation without any discrepancy in estimated phasor value, irrespective of different manufacturers. This paper presents a comparative analysis of fundamental phasor estimation algorithms namely Basic FFT, Recursive DFT and Non-Recursive DFT under normal operating condition and in presence of noise and harmonics.

articleTitle: The promise of DSM in smart grid using home energy management system with renewable integration
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The increase in energy consumption, its environmental impact and limits in generation illustrate the important of energy savings and alternate usage as renewable energy sources. The main objective is to optimize payment cost of the customer. We have conducted different case studies in order to identify the strength of the proposed method and investigation the impacts of different electrical hours based tariffs on the results optimization on daily basis. This paper proposed the suitability of approaches to modelling DSM for renewables integration in the HEMS.

articleTitle: An efficient hop selection model to enhance lifetime of wireless sensor network
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is composed of small and low-cost sensor devices which are battery powered and are deployed in non-rechargeable location. Therefore preserving the energy of these resource constrained sensor devices is most desired. Recently co-operative communication has attained wide interest and has been adopted by various clustering approaches which is a potential solution to preserve energy of these devices. These techniques are not efficient in enhancing the lifetime of sensor network since they considered minimizing energy consumption per bit only. To address this, here we present a distributed MAC (Medium Access control) transceiver optimization for hop selection. The proposed model minimizes the energy consumption and maximizes the lifetime of sensor network. Experimental results shows significant performance improvement over existing approach in terms of life enhancement.

articleTitle: Energy data analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Energy audit program is an ongoing strategy for controlling building energy consumptions. The recent crises/ burden related to environmental impacts are increasing effectively and it draws attention towards utilization of solar energy. Data-driven techniques based on the operational parameters as inputs and corresponding predictive analytics measures for energy consumption as the outcome. The process of Analyzing is to break down the complex objects into simpler forms for achieving the goals. The use of R statistical tool has become more prominent mode of analyzing huge quantity of data. Auditing incorporates the principles of sustainable designs and energy efficient solutions for building projects mainly seeks to locate, design, construct and service operations to reduce negative impact on environment and consumption of natural resources.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of abnormal heartbeat using wavelet transform
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Nowadays bio medical signal processing is annewly emerging active research area spanning several domains. Biomedical signals originate from physiological activities of organisms, ranging from gene to tissue and organ images. These signal processing aims at extracting more meaningful information from biomedical signals. With the aid of biomedical signal processing, with this physicians can diagnose distinct illnesses more promptly[2]. This paper describes easyand convenient diagnosis (normal or abnormal)of heartbeat using frequency domain technique. The more powerful transform technique which is exploited to detect abnormal heart beat is Wavelet Transform. Thus transform subdivides the signal into four subbands and provides simultaneously both time and frequency domain information. The statistical parameters like entropy, histogram, mean, mode and range are computed for heartbeat signal by Discrete Wavelet Transform and Wavelet Packet Transform. The hypothesis is that these parameters determine the abnormalities present in the heartbeat and physician can decide the person's health condition.

articleTitle: Out-of-step technique based symmetrical fault analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: During the normal condition of the power system, power flows through the line in nominal frequency. Sometimes the disturbances occur due to sudden load change or due to any fault in the transmission line. So during the recovery of the system electromechanical oscillation is there in the power system network which results in power swing, this encourages undesirable tripping or cascade tripping of line causes the power system blackouts. To avoid this situation like blackouts, Here current differential protection scheme and the phasor difference analysis between two bus power system is analyzed to detect the fault during out-of-step condition accurately.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of bridgeless PFC buck boost converter fed BLDC motor drive
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In this work, a new PFC (Power Factor Correction) Bridgeless Buck-Boost converter is designed and proposed for BLDC (Brushless Direct Current) Motor Drive applications. In this topology, two power electronic devices are used to control negative and positive cycles of input single phase supply. This alternately controls the input DC voltage of the inverter. Speed control of BLDC machine is achieved by varying the inverter DC link voltage. In this design, inverter consists of only two legs instead of three legs and third phase of the motor is connected to the midpoint of capacitors and inverter is operating at fundamental switching frequency. This topology is designed to operate in DICM mode (Discontinuous Inductor Current Mode) to provide an inherent power factor correction at input AC supply side. Proposed circuit is modeled in Matlab/Simulink tool by using Simpower system and Xilinx block set.

articleTitle: Simple architecture for smart home using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Home Security is a critical issue in today's life when everyone is staying outside for either personal or professional reason. It becomes difficult for them to keep track of the happenings at home. They are extremely particular about who is entering their house when they are outside and deciding who should enter into the home. There are system installed in houses to ensure the security of the house like alarms and video cameras they do not provide end to end security and are less focused on heterogeneous environment w.r.to protocols and standards they use can't be integrated within the solution. This work aims to provide a secure, efficient and reliable system that can help users to keep track of happenings at their home or even in their office. This system informs the user about the visitor whose entry can be restricted by the owner irrespective of the location. This work proposes a framework using Internet of Things that includes intelligence in networking while sending data to the user. Inclusion of intelligent network within the system makes this framework robust for fast and efficient communication from end device to cloud and vice versa. This framework would provide a uniform access to devices and information and would facilitate different kind of interactions among them. The framework would ensure end to end security, management and automation within the system with reduces delay and enhances reliability.

articleTitle: A 1-V high-gain two-stage self-cascode operational transconductance amplifier
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper presents design of two-stage operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using self-cascode MOSFET to achieve high gain with a low-supply voltage. To improve the gain of OTA a positive feedback is created by cross coupling the bulk terminals of the input stage load transistors. The proposed design is implemented in a standard 65 nm CMOS process with a supply voltage of 1 V. The designed self-cascode OTA affords a DC gain of 78 dB, unity gain frequency of 191 MHz and a phase margin of 63.5° with a small process, voltage, temperature (PVT) variations.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimal economic emission power dispatch using Bat algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper presents Bat Algorithm based on Environmental and Economy using multi-objective thermal power Dispatch problem which is articulated as a non-inferior solution to the multi-objective problem. The proposed algorithm minimizes both fuel cost and emission simultaneously. Simulation outcomes presented for the standard IEEE 30-bus system using the Bat Algorithm with Weighted Sum are compared to other former approaches. The combustion of fossil fuel gives rise to particular material and gaseous pollutants apart from the discharge of heat to water courses as by-products. Several contaminants, such as Sulphur oxides, nitrogen oxides and carbon dioxide shows destructive effects on human life. In the Multi-objective problem formulation, there is minimum emission dispatch for in operating strategy, which can ensure minimum pollution level at minimum operating cost. The proposed procedure proves to be dealing competitive in the field of evolutionary algorithms on multi objective optimization problems in comparison with other algorithms.

articleTitle: Browshing a new way of phishing using a malicious browser extension
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Phishing is a well-known cybercrime. It is performed using various tricks and techniques including email spoofing, exploiting browser vulnerabilities, web spoofing, DNS poisoning, etc. This paper sheds light on a new technique that can be used by attackers to perform a successful phishing attack through malicious browser extensions. Successful experiments have been performed over the Google Chrome browser and the technique has been validated. This paper will help researchers and browser development companies to understand this specific phishing attack and to focus on research in the area of detection and mitigation of this phishing attack.

articleTitle: Design and tuning of PIλDμ controller for higher order process using PSO-NM
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: FOPID controller is more vigorous and has better control performance than conventional PID controller because it has two more degree of freedom. There has been an increase in applications of FOPID controller in recent years because of increase in research efforts in fractional calculus. In this paper a method for tuning of parameters of fractional order PID controller for higher order process is proposed by combining the properties of a stochastic (PSO) and a deterministic (NELDER-MEAD) optimization technique, which is minimizing ISE. The results are compared with traditional Ziegler and Nichols type critical gain based tuning rules, Nelder-Mead and PSO based optimisation algorithm for higher order systems. FOPID controller is utilized using FOMCON based toolbox. Two higher order plants are taken for demonstration of better result.

articleTitle: Characterization of virgin and aged transformer oil with SiO2 nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The transformer is one of the key components of the power system. Transformer oil forms an essential part of its insulation system. It provides dielectric strength along with cooling properties. This paper aims to embark upon the promises shown by nanofluids, by dispersing 0.01% mass fraction of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles in virgin and naturally aged transformer oil. Their effect on the dominant attributes, namely, AC breakdown strength, density, viscosity, flash point and fire point has been tested. Weibull analysis has been utilized to model the probability distribution of AC breakdown voltage. Both the types of nanooil, exhibit superior dielectric strength compared to their base oil. The increment in density is minor, while no clear pattern is followed in terms of the results of viscosity test. The flash point and fire point values show a significant increment in case of virgin oil based nanooil, while in the case of aged oil base, the increment is minor.

articleTitle: High voltage control of power system by changing generator transformer tap positions case study
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: This paper presents a case study to control high voltage in power system with changing tap position of generator transformer. Rajasthan power system having two 765 kV GSS, twenty one 400 kV GSS and seven thermal plants have been selected to carry out case study and simulated in PSSE software. Simulation model consists of 85 buses, 62 transmission lines and 86 transformers. Total system load is 5656.60 MW & 907.02 MVAR. Five cases have been simulated considering the effect of generator transformer tap position on power system voltage and generator MVAR loading. From simulation studies it is found out that transmission network voltage profile is significantly reduced with increase of generator transformer tap position and injection of reactive power in National Grid is significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of energy efficient protocols for wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Advances in I/W/EoT (Internet, Web, Everything of Things) based smart environments have created huge demand in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). These smart environments require energy efficient hardware and software due to nature of wireless communication and constraints of sensors incorporated in the system. “IEEE 802.15.4” standard is used for wireless medium access and data transmission at physical layer (PHY) and Medium Access Control (MAC) layer. It provides MAC sublayer which may work in beacon-enabled or non-beacon-enabled modes. The case study based focused approach provides better understanding of IoT applications with useful insights of hardware and software technologies. In this paper IoE based home automation system is simulated for understanding architecture of IoE based environments. “IEEE 802.15.4” protocol is analyzed using simulation using “contiki-os” and “cooja” simulator environment. The data generated by simulation is analyzed using packet capturing tool for identifying the nature of wireless communication and protocols involved in WSN. Factors affecting IPv6 packet transfers in WSN using “IEEE 802.15.4” and 6LoWPAN protocol is analyzed using simulation.

articleTitle: Design and operational constraints of NEA +800kV, 6000MW UHVDC bipolar system
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: The world's first 800kV 6000MW HVDC Multiterminal project of North East to Agra has been commissioned in September 2015. This particular line traverses 1728 km from Biswanath Chariali in Assam-Alipurduar in West Bengal-Agra. This NEA 800kV project had been developed stage-wise using parallel groups of converters in which each pole has continuous power overload capacity of 33%. The indoor DC Hall (75 m × 75 m and 40 m height) containing Smoothing reactors, DC filters, DC dis-connectors and other DC equipments have been provided to protect HVDC equipments from environmental pollution. Main Objective of this paper is to understand the basic operation of the bipolar UHVDC scheme, To study the basic coupling scheme adopted in North East Agra, To analyze the converter operation and to design the total HVDC Bipolar scheme in some particular software i.e. AUTOCAD and analyze the operation of these bipolar scheme.

articleTitle: Novel closed loop control for power factor correction using magnetic energy recovery switch
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Poor power factor is one of the major issues in electrical energy system. This manuscript presents a technology called Magnetic Energy Recovery Switch (MERS) for improvement of power factor and compensation of reactive power demanded by the load. Basically MERS act as a voltage source and variable capacitor connected in series which can compensate the inductive reactance of the system. A new/modified closed loop control strategy is proposed in this paper. The control scheme is free from phase locked loop (PLL) and zero crossing detector (ZCD). The effectiveness of closed loop control is verified on MATLAB/Simulink environment. Variable resistive-inductive load is used for creating the reactive power demand in the system. The load is varied at different time instant and the reliability of the closed loop control for tracing the unity power factor is verified.

articleTitle: Study and analysis of hadoop cluster optimization based on configuration properties
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: Hadoop framework consists of multiple components. One set of configuration parameters may not be suitable for all types of applications. Hence, for optimum performance, each framework parameter needs to be carefully chosen and adjusted. This paper highlights some of the important configuration properties related to Block size, memory allocation, CPU allocation, Number of MapReduce jobs, Job scheduling and JVM which should be tuned for improved Hadoop application performance. The result of some Benchmark problems are analyzed.

articleTitle: Occupant comfort analysis of an educational building located in warm-humid tropical climate
publicationTitle: 2017 Innovations in Power and Advanced Computing Technologies (i-PACT)
abstract: In this modern era, the demand for electrical energy is increasing drastically in accordance with time. This increasing demand is not met by the present day generation, creating an energy shortage in the Indian power system. Hence, it is the hour to think for an immediate strategy to preserve energy for the future. Also every kind of energy use applications in a building are primarily meant for providing comfort to its occupants. A proper energy audit in the existing buildings and implementing corrective actions so as to reduce the energy consumption is one of the important measure to cop up with the increasing energy demand. Occupant comfort is one of the major criteria that is to be assessed for rating a building. Visual comfort and thermal comfort are important while considering the occupant comfort. Lighting and cooling are the important energy consuming sectors to be considered in a building located in an area having hot and humid tropical climate. This paper presents the analysis of visual comfort and thermal comfort in a typical educational building complex located in hot and humid climate zone. The results obtained as a part of the energy audit conducted for the building complex are studied on the basis of different standards.
